proofs.text: Write `#!/bin/sh\necho mine\n` into `.git/hooks/pre-push`, run init and verify the file is unchanged and the output says `add this line to it`; on a second project write `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, run init and verify the output names the pre-commit framework and `.git/hooks/pre-push` was not written

reasons: PROOF-26 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: A pre-push hook someone else wrote, or a repository whose hooks another tool manages, is named in the summary with the line to add rather than written over

tests.body:
def test_a_hook_someone_else_wrote_is_kept(self, project):
        write(project.path('.git/hooks/pre-push'), '#!/bin/sh\necho mine\n')
        output = project.run('--gate', 'tested')
        assert read(project.path('.git/hooks/pre-push')) == \
            '#!/bin/sh\necho mine\n'
        assert 'add this line to it' in output
tests.name: test_a_hook_manager_is_named_rather_than_written_over
